ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Overhaul
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The core of this modlist: a medieval tech tree, raw materials to process, and a new world
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Logs and ore need working before you can build with them. Plan the workshops first.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Overhaul rebuilds RimWorld around the Middle Ages: its own Medieval research tab, raw materials that must be worked before you can use them, rustic furniture, castle walls, siege engines, and a world of noble houses, brigands, cultists and monsters. Almost everything else in this modlist is balanced around it, so learn its production chains before your first winter.

li.heading: The production chains
li.text: Four kinds of raw material have to be worked before you can build or craft with them. Each chain can be switched off in the mod's settings. Open them before you start: you can turn off any chain you find tedious, stop torches from needing fuel, and remove hornet nests from new maps.

table.li: Chain | Raw material | Worked into
Wood | raw wood, from trees | wood planks, sawn at a trestle; later a windmill or watermill does it without labor
Leather | hides, from animals | leather at the tanning rack, which burns tanning liquor you boil from wood at a campfire or stove; or stiff rawhide at the rawhide rack, which needs no liquor
Cloth | plant fibers | cloth or linen, by spinning
Metal | ore | ingots, smelted at the furnace. Steel no longer comes out of the ground: iron ingots are refined into steel once you finish the Steel research, which needs Alchemy first.

li.after: Set up the wood chain before anything else. Research Leather Tanning early and keep tanning liquor in stock, or the hides from every hunt pile up unused.

li.heading: Research and schematics
li.text:
Some research projects need a schematic scroll, and the scroll must sit in a bookcase in the same room as the research bench. Schematics turn up in ruins and with caravans that trade them, and they gate weapons, cooking and metallurgy. Put a bookcase in your research room, store schematics there, and buy every schematic a caravan offers.
Mining, the windmill, the watermill, the ballista and the trebuchet can only be researched at the advanced research bench, which Engineering unlocks.

li.heading: Plowing and the messenger table
li.text:
With Plowed Soil researched you can plow fields for extra fertility. By default plowed soil can wear out after a harvest, and new plowing is planned for you automatically.
The messenger table and a linked bird post work as the medieval comms console: talk to factions, call for trade and ask for help.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council detects a medieval colony automatically and doesn't count the watermill's river gauge as electricity. It recognizes this mod's buildings by what they do: rustic torches and oil lamps count as lights, log and straw beds as beds, and the smoker, drying racks, apiary, banners, fountains and weapon rack fulfill the matching wishes.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Overhaul: food and drink
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Bread, smoked meat, cheese, ale, wine and mead, and how to keep them coming
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Wine and cheese get better the longer they sit.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Overhaul turns the kitchen into a small economy. Wheat becomes flour and flour becomes bread; meat is smoked or dried so it keeps without a freezer; milk is pressed into cheese; grain, grapes and honey become ale, wine and mead in barrels. Good food and drink are the cheapest mood a medieval colony can buy, and aged wine is one of the few luxuries you can make yourself.

li.heading: Brewing
li.text:
At the brewery, 25 wheat make 5 ale wort, and the wort turns into ale in a fermenting barrel in 6 days. Wine needs grape must and mead needs honey. Apple juice turns into cider on its own when kept at room temperature.
Barrels work between -1 and 32 °C and best from 7 °C up. Below 7 °C they slow down sharply; above 32 °C the brew starts to spoil. Dig a cellar for them and keep it between 7 and 32 °C all year. The fermenting barrel that makes ale, wine and mead costs iron ingots, so smelt some first.

li.heading: Aging wine, mead and cheese
li.text: Wine, mead and cheese age toward a target quality you pick on the barrel or press. The higher the target, the longer the wait:

table.li: Target quality | Days to age
Normal | 8
Good | 14
Excellent | 20
Masterwork | 50
Legendary | 120

li.after: A glass of wine or mead, or a slice of cheese, gives a mood for a day by its quality: from -7 for awful to +15 for legendary. A mug of ale gives +4. Age everyday wine and cheese to good or excellent, and start a few casks toward legendary well before a planned wedding or feast.

li.heading: Meat that keeps

table.li: Building | Makes | Time | Keeps for
Smoker | smoked meat, a small meal | a day | 30 days
Drying rack | dried meat, a cooking ingredient | two and a half days | 60 days

li.after: Both work on raw meat. Smoke and dry meat in autumn so it keeps through winter, and save the freezer for vegetables.

li.heading: Bread, honey and slop
li.text:
Wheat takes 12 days to harvest, so grow it early, and research the windmill or watermill: they grind flour and saw planks without a worker. The apiary makes honeycomb about every 5 days while it is between 13 and 37 °C, and rests at night.
Slop pots are the medieval paste dispenser: the plain pot serves slop, the ragout pot stew and the fondue pot a fine cheese fondue.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text:
The council counts this mod's barrel as a fermenter for brewery wishes and the brewery room plan, and ale, wine, mead and cider all count as something to drink. The firewood wish counts both raw wood and planks, so a full woodpile of either settles a colonist worried about the coming frost.
The mod's dishes and drinks leave memories of their own, and Rimfolk's journals pick them up: a day with apple pie or griffon berry pie, hunter's stew, a bowl of slop, the colony's cheese or wine (good or turned, as the quality says), ale and mead, smoked meat and sausages, or an hour in a decent library can be the day's entry. Visitors notice the colony's crafts once it has them: they taste its cheese, talk wine by the barrels, warm themselves at the hearth, wait by the oven for bread, stand among the hives in summer and ask to see the scribe's table and the books.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Overhaul: houses, monsters and sieges
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Noble houses, brigands, cultists, trolls and golems, and the trebuchets they bring
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Check a new map for odd iron or silver formations before anyone starts mining.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Overhaul fills the world with four noble houses, brigands and a hidden cult, and the wilds with beasts out of Battle Brothers: trolls, lindwurms, griffons, direwolves, unholds and golems. Medieval factions besiege you with trebuchets instead of mortars, and ruins and cult hideouts are worth exploring if you go well armed.

li.heading: Houses, brigands and cultists
li.text:
The noble houses are House Amboise, House Soren (merchants), House Oswin (ruin delvers) and House Hesse, a cruel house that starts out hostile.
Brigands and the Cultists have no towns you can visit; they guard ruins and hideouts. The explorer's workbench pieces torn notes together into the locations of cultist hideouts in three sizes. Keep the Cultists faction switched on when you create the world, or their hideouts and the loot in them never appear.

li.heading: Sieges
li.text: Medieval factions besiege with trebuchets and lines of wooden cavalry spikes instead of mortars, and arrive from the sky by balloon instead of drop pod. A trebuchet is built to smash walls from beyond bow range, so when one goes up, go out and break it quickly.

points.li: Rare daers, lindwurms, griffons and ancient trolls sometimes wander in and leave after a while. Let trolls and lindwurms go unless you are ready: trolls regenerate their wounds, so a slow fight favors them. A griffon or daer hunted with a full company pays well in hides and horns.
A strange meteorite can crash down with dormant golems inside, which are a serious threat.

Unusual iron or silver formations on a new map hide golems too, and mining them wakes what is inside. Read the map before you mine, and leave humming iron formations alone until your fighters are home.
Working a mine shaft can wake insects under the ground, the same way a deep drill does.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A beast that mauls a colonist and gets away can become a named nemesis, and a house that kills one of yours can earn a vendetta. The council's defense advice counts cavalry spikes as traps, but not manned ballistas as turrets.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Overhaul: Royalty
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The Empire as a medieval power: knights, fortresses, medieval permits and noble armor
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The medieval Empire still expects throne rooms and the right clothes.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: This add-on gives Royalty's Empire a medieval face. Its soldiers march in plate and carry swords, its settlements are fortresses, its traders sell medieval goods, and its permits fit a world without aerodrones. It also lets Medieval Overhaul's finest armor count as noble apparel, so a knight can dress for the title without spacer cloth.

li.heading: Knights and fortresses
li.text: Imperial troops become peasants, mercenaries, light and heavy infantry, grenadiers, crusaders and the praetorian guard, all in medieval gear. With Giddy-Up the Empire also fields mounted crusaders. Imperial settlements are fortresses, so attacking one takes siege gear.

li.heading: Permits and titles
li.text:
The glitterworld medicine, aerodrone strike and aerodrone salvo permits are gone; a request for herbal medicine takes their place. Plan on herbal medicine from the Empire rather than glitterworld kits, and keep your own doctor and medicine stocked.
Medieval Overhaul plate armor and great helms count toward a title's apparel requirements, full plate, armets and great helms among them. Dress your nobles in Medieval Overhaul's adorned or gilded plate: it covers the apparel demand and protects them in a raid.
Every part of the mod can be switched off on its own, and its settings list what each title needs in its throne room and bedroom. Read that rank overview before accepting a promotion, then build for the next title, not this one.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Titled colonists still ask for a room befitting their title, and the council's throne room plan and royalty pages apply as usual.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Overhaul add-ons
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Toggleable Stuff, Barbarians and Air Vehicles: smaller mods built on Medieval Overhaul
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A full set of barbarian armor takes eighteen skulls.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Three add-ons that hang off Medieval Overhaul. Toggleable Stuff adds and switches small conveniences, Barbarians brings a skull-and-plunder way of life, and Air Vehicles puts hot air balloons and airships in a medieval sky.

li.heading: Toggleable Stuff
li.text: Each option has its own switch and needs a restart:

points.li: A loading cart that works like a trade beacon. Turn it on and park it next to your trade goods so visiting traders can see them.
A thermostat on the stove and hearth.

li.heading: Barbarians
li.text: A barbarian faction and way of life: you loot enemy gear and rework it into barbarian armor and weapons with skulls, up to 18 for a full outfit. It also adds 14 weapons, shields, banners and the northern horse. For a barbarian run the author suggests a tribal start; research the barbarian projects and plan your raids around the skulls you need.

li.heading: Air Vehicles

table.li: Vehicle | Carries
Hot air balloon | a pilot, one passenger and 150 kg of cargo
Airship | a pilot, ten passengers and 1000 kg

li.after: Both burn coal. Their research opens after Engineering, and the airship also needs a special book. A balloon is a cheap scout and a quick way to reach a nearby quest; keep coal stocked at home for the trip back.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Colonists away in a balloon or airship are still counted as part of the colony, and a barbarian banner counts for the wish to fly the colony's colors.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Rimedieval
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Keeps the whole world medieval: no guns, no mechanoids, no high-tech events
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: No mechanoids, no orbital traders, no toxic fallout. Raids, disease and winter are still there.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Rimedieval does not delete technology; it hides it. Research beyond the medieval era disappears from your tree, every faction and pawn from every mod is re-equipped with medieval or neolithic gear, and the events and quests that only make sense in a spacer world are removed. It is the reason a raider in this modlist carries a crossbow instead of a charge rifle.

li.heading: The research limit
li.text: Your research is limited to the medieval era. The setting "Allow pre-industrial tech" widens it to industrial projects up to electricity, but not microelectronics or anything that needs it.

li.heading: What disappears

points.li: Mechanoids are disabled by default: any that appear are destroyed, and they stop being hostile.
Events: toxic fallout, volcanic winter, psychic drones and soothes, short circuits, mech clusters, ship part crashes, ship chunks, orbital traders and the ship-escape ending.
Ancient junk and mech remains no longer generate on maps, and plasteel and compacted machinery no longer appear as ore.
Buildings from other mods that are too advanced are taken out of the build menu instead of being deleted.
The comms console becomes a signal fire.

li.after: Research and build the signal fire early, or Medieval Overhaul's messenger table and bird post, so you can call traders and allies.

li.heading: Load order and factions
li.text: The author recommends loading Rimedieval near the bottom of the list. If modded raiders ever arrive with guns, move it further down. If the Vanilla Expanded framework asks whether to add Rimedieval's factions, don't; the author warns against it.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Events Rimedieval removes stay removed, and dream omens will not bring them back. Buildings it hides are never suggested, and with mechanoids disabled, dreams and life goals about them never come up.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: RimFantasy: Medieval Overhaul Edition
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Gem magic: arcane weapons, magical lights and climate control, and the legacy of House Doyle
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Most of the magic here runs on gems, so keep some in stock.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: RimFantasy adds gem magic to Medieval Overhaul's world: magical weapons with powers, magical furniture for light and for temperature, and magical defenses for your colony. House Doyle builds on it with amethyst as a new resource, amethyst jewelry, craftable heraldic weapons and armor, and arcane weapons made with amethyst; some arcane weapons can only be found through exploration. Gems feed the jewelry, the magical furniture and the arcane weapons, so mine and trade for them.

li.heading: Before you load them
li.text:
Both are rebuilt to Medieval Overhaul's standards and replace the original RimFantasy series, which must not be loaded with them.
The authors list a moderate incompatibility with Simple Sidearms, which is in this modlist: it breaks the no-bond rules of arcane weapons. If arcane weapons misbehave with sidearms, turn on "Allow use of blocked weapons" in Simple Sidearms' settings, as the author suggests.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council recognizes lights and heaters by what they do, so magical lamps and climate furniture count like torches and hearths. The jewelry wish looks for rings, necklaces, bracelets, amulets and the like.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Total Rim
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Medieval II: Total War in RimWorld: the core, armory, animals, quests and prosthetics
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Foreign horse breeds only come from foreign traders.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Total Rim brings the factions of Medieval II: Total War into RimWorld, built to sit beside Medieval Overhaul and the Tasty Armory mods. The core holds the shared ideologies, cultures and backstories; the other modules add armor, historical animal breeds, quests with real choices and pre-industrial prosthetics. The nations themselves come in their own packs.

li.heading: The modules

table.li: Module | What it adds

Core | The shared memes, fixed ideologies, backstories and code for the nation packs, and the Teutonic Order, a permanent hostile military order. It also makes Tasty Armory's shields usable without Combat Extended.
Armory | 4 engraved armor variants, 7 hats and 23 helmets, and patches that bring Tasty Armory's items in line with Medieval Overhaul's stats.

Animals | Historical dog, cat and horse breeds. Wild ones such as the caracal and the Iberian lynx live in their biomes; breeds like the Andalusian horse or the Chartreux cat are only sold by their nation's traders.
Quests and Incidents | Five quests where you pick a side or an approach, and two random events that can lift moods or bring trade, but may also spread disease.
Pre-Industrial Prosthetics | Three sets of prosthetics with their own research, better than a peg leg but below industrial bionics.

li.after: Read each quest's options before you commit, because the approach you pick changes the rewards on offer. Buy horse breeds and pets from each nation's traders when they visit, and research the prosthetics before your first big battle, so a colonist who loses a hand can still work.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A colonist who loses a limb asks for a prosthetic once you can make one, and these count.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Total Rim: the nations
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: France, the Holy Roman Empire, Poland, Muscovy, the Mongols, the Ottomans, Byzantium and Iberia
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Six nations, Byzantium and three Iberian factions share the world map.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Each nation pack adds a faction inspired by Medieval II: Total War. Together they turn the world map into a crowded medieval Europe and beyond, with neighbors that each have their own armies and beliefs.

li.heading: The packs
li.text:
Six packs add a single nation each: the Kingdom of France, the Holy Roman Empire, the Kingdom of Poland, the Grand Principality of Moscow, the Mongolian Khaganate and the Ottoman Empire. The Eastern Roman Empire pack adds Byzantium and is built to work with Royalty as well. Reconquista adds three Iberian factions, Spain, Portugal and the Moors, with two ideologies between them.
Every pack adds new unit types, backstories, a culture, an ideology and scenarios you can start with. The rosters use gear from all the Tasty Armory mods, which is why they are all required.

li.heading: Living next to them
li.text: A nation scenario gives you a colony that starts with a culture and an ideology already in place. Look at a nation's ideology before you recruit its prisoners, because people bring their beliefs with them. Trade with the nations for their horses, pets and armor; each sells things the others do not.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Their visitors and traders meet your colonists like any others, and a nation whose raiders kill one of yours can earn a vendetta.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Divine Order
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: A zealous knightly order, its sacred tablets, its arms and armor, and its warhorses
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The Order distrusts outsiders, but it will still sell you a warhorse.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Divine Order adds a medieval fantasy faction of iron-clad zealots who see it as their mission to cleanse the realm of corruption. They distrust outsiders but sometimes make uneasy alliances. With them come their weapons and armor, sacred tablets, a new altar and sculptures, a warhorse and a scenario for players who have stolen from them.

li.heading: Tablets and warhorses
li.text:
Sacred tablets must be studied for the elite armor research and are also a crafting component, so study your first one before you use any in crafting. You can trade for them, take them from crusaders, inquisitors and heralds, or rarely win one from a quest. The scenario "Divine Order defectors" starts you with four defectors on the run with a stolen sacred tablet.
The Order's warhorse is larger, stronger and faster than a regular horse. The Order and merchant caravans sell it, so buy one when they have it.

li.heading: With other mods in this list
li.text: With EBSG Framework, which this modlist has, the Order's weapons deal extra damage to Anomaly entities. With Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes, also in this modlist, the faction carries the Violent Conversion meme. The author notes that Rimedieval may give the Order's pawns different weapons and apparel than intended, so expect a few odd loadouts.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: An altar of any style counts for a colonist's wish for a place to pray.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Fantasy themed rewards, resources and relics
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Spacer rewards, rare materials and relic quests renamed and redrawn for a fantasy world
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The shield talisman is a shield belt with a new name and picture.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Three companion mods that keep the game's high-tech rewards but dress them for a medieval fantasy world. Nothing is added or removed: items work as before under new names, descriptions and pictures, so a quest reward reads like treasure instead of a spaceship part. Read a reward by its effect, not its name: a "healing potion" is the old healer mech serum and just as precious.

table.li: In vanilla | Renamed | Mod
Persona weapons | possessed weapons | Quest Rewards
Shield belt | shield talisman | Quest Rewards
Luciferium | demon blood potion | Quest Rewards
Glitterworld medicine | exalted medicine | Quest Rewards
Skilltrainers | skill tomes | Quest Rewards
Psytrainers | spell tomes | Quest Rewards
Launchers and targeters | staffs and spell scrolls | Quest Rewards
Plasteel | mithril | Rare Resources
Uranium | adamantite | Rare Resources
Synthread | damask | Rare Resources
Hyperweave | runeweave | Rare Resources
Ideology's relic and ancient complex quests | ancient outposts with sarcophagi, treasure chests and ancient texts | Relic Quests
Hacking | investigating | Relic Quests
Shuttles and drop pods | airships and balloons, everywhere | Relic Quests

li.heading: Rimedieval and the rewards
li.text: The rewards are set to the medieval tech level so Rimedieval does not filter them out, except the shield talisman and barrier spell scroll as quest rewards. With Relic Quests active, Rimedieval lets the ancient complex quests back into the game, so if your ideology wants a relic, take the relic quests when they come up.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Skill tomes and spell tomes count as books when a reader asks for more on the shelves. The Almanac's pages still use the vanilla names, so glitterworld medicine there means exalted medicine here.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval Medicines (Medieval Overhaul Edition)
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Three tiers of medieval medicine, four tiers of prosthetics, potions and a medieval cryptosleep
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Keep some of the ale back for the doctor.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Medicines fills the long gap between herbal medicine and industrial kits. It adds tiered medicines made from herbs, cloth and alcohol, prosthetic limbs from a crude hook up to emerald-enchanted Paresian limbs, healing and mana potions, and Entosomnia, a medieval stand-in for the cryptosleep casket.

li.heading: The medicines

table.li: Medicine | Made from
Early medieval | herbal medicine and cloth or linen
Late medieval | adds alcohol; made at the alchemy bench
Paresian | neutroamine, late medicine, mithril and cloth

li.after: They range from slightly better than herbal medicine to slightly better than industrial medicine. The late medieval recipe accepts Medieval Overhaul's drinks, so turn spare ale and wine into medicine. Watch your doctors for a day after adding the mod: if pawns don't use these medicines on their own, the author suggests the Mod Medicines Patch.

li.heading: Limbs and potions
li.text:
Prosthetics come in four tiers: crude, artificial, mechanical and Paresian. The first three top out at 80% efficiency. Paresian limbs, made with emeralds at the alchemy bench, match a natural limb, and Paresian eyes and ears restore sight and hearing. Keep a few emeralds back: one restored hand can bring a master crafter back to work.
Lesser and minor healing potions speed healing with some drawbacks. Mana potions restore psyfocus and need Royalty.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: These medicines count toward a well-stocked infirmary, and a colonist missing a limb asks for any prosthetic the colony can make.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: DBH for Medieval
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Medieval pumps, toilets, baths and water treatment for Dubs Bad Hygiene
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: With this add-on, wells, pipes and a bathhouse need no power.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Dubs Bad Hygiene has little to offer before electricity. This add-on gives a medieval colony its own plumbing: pumps, toilets, baths and water purification buildable with medieval technology, and water pipes that connect to primitive wells. It is not built for Dubs Bad Hygiene Lite; the full version's Lite mode option works instead.

li.heading: With Medieval Overhaul
li.text: The add-on is patched for Medieval Overhaul. The log boiler and fueled sauna heater also burn coal, wind pumps need the Windmill research, and steel and components in medieval-tier costs become iron ingots and basic components. Stock coal from the charcoal pile or a mine for the boiler and sauna heater before winter.

li.heading: Wells and latrines
li.text: Connect your well to pipes early; carrying water by hand takes hours of work. Keep latrines and septic tanks away from wells, kitchens and the hospital.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: A bathtub or hot tub fulfills the wish of someone who has not been properly clean in a long time; a water tub or a sauna doesn't.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: RimTraits - Medieval Talents
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Every pawn gets one talent trait, from common to very rare
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A talented doctor without a passion for medicine still treats patients well.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Medieval Talents gives every pawn exactly one talent: a trait that says what they are naturally good at, separate from what they enjoy. Talents also toughen people up against cold, heat, pain and breakdowns, to make up for living without modern comforts.

li.heading: How talents work
li.text:
The mod adds 35 talent traits. Every pawn gets exactly one, and they are mutually exclusive; the higher a talent's tier, the rarer it is. Talents can also give bonuses to temperature tolerance, mood, mental break threshold and pain tolerance. The author balanced it for big medieval colonies of 50 or more people.
Read the talent on every recruit and prisoner: a rare talent is often worth more than a high skill. Give work by talent and passion together. A talented colonist without passion still works well, just without enjoying it.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The council does not read talents yet. Life goals and wishes still come from passions, traits and what happens to people.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: Medieval styles, walls and wardrobe
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Medieval Walls, the Dwarven and Greekcore styles, The Wild Fields and a medieval Misc. Training
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A ditch slows the raiders; an embrasure covers the archer shooting at them.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Smaller mods that change how a medieval colony looks and what it wears. Two of them change play a little: Medieval Walls adds embrasures and ditches for defense, and The Wild Fields adds noble clothes and weapons. The rest are styles and retextures.

li.heading: Medieval Walls
li.text: The walls and embrasures cost twice a normal wall and are a bit sturdier. Embrasures give 75% cover, and cellar ditches slow attackers a lot and can be dug on any floor. Ring your gate with ditches and line the wall with embrasures: raiders slow down exactly where your archers can see them.

li.heading: The Wild Fields
li.text: Adds 7 garments and 4 weapons inspired by Polish nobility and the Cossacks. With Medieval Overhaul they fit its weapon tiers; with Royalty the noble pieces satisfy noble apparel needs.

li.heading: Styles and retextures

points.li: Stoneborn - Dwarven Style Pack: an Ideology style for dwarven colonies, with styled furniture, altars, sculptures, weapons and helmets, hall pillars and doors, dwarven floors and its own ritual.
Gerrymon's Greekcore Style: Greek clothing and laurels, the klinai (a couch you can sleep on that doesn't make a bedroom), a carved stone fence and marble tiles that count as fine floors.
Misc. Training Medieval Retexture: gives Misc. Training's dummies and targets a medieval look and changes their materials. It must load after Misc. Training.

li.after: Pick a style when you set up your ideology: styles change how your buildings and gear look, and believers like rooms where their style dominates.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: Training dummies and archery targets fulfill a fighter's wish for somewhere to train, and any styled altar counts as a place to pray.
